criteria.rationale: Verified the shared five-tool implementation, process-local signing and full-scan disclosure. Restart invalidation and platform-specific metadata limitations are explicit design limits. Cross-platform execution was not independently verified.
Focused tests passed with -race in internal/pose and internal/mcpserver. Signing-key initialization and generation-cache access are synchronized; no retained query lifecycle is introduced.
All five MCP tools use the shared cursor contract. Version-1 tokens are explicitly refused, legacy unpaginated calls remain supported, and pagination metadata is additive.
Hostile tokens, altered bindings, expiry, positions, null cursors, argument aliases and invalid explicit limits have negative coverage. Focused tests passed independently.
Handlers integrate the domain cursor helper, generation-reader status and shared schema. The strict surface check passed with one delivery target and zero findings.
Pages disclose generation status, reason, diverged files, collection, position, total and full-scan cost. Cursor refusals provide bounded codes and restart guidance without exposing signing material.
The token migration is explicit. Calls omitting pagination remain unpaginated; continuations are bounded. The CLI has no cursor-paginated surface requiring migration.

Independent focused and race-enabled tests passed, as did go vet. Collection mutation, query binding, generation metadata, limits and token failures have relevant coverage; sealed build and unit evidence also pass.

Binding the signed cursor to the ordered collection and query removes the cause of silent offset drift. Recomputing and refusing changed collections implements the selected restart strategy without snapshot retention.

criteria.rationale: The operational documentation, translations, scaffold copies, ADR and tool descriptions agree on signed cursors, restart behavior, the 500-item bound and collection disclosure. Full-scan cost is explicit in the runtime contract and spec.

The implementation binds generation, query, filters, ordering and project/root scope; detects changed collections; bounds tokens and pages; discloses scan cost; and preserves current gate authority. Index-backed work reduction is an owned follow-up because these collections are not indexed.
Cursor errors distinguish malformed, unsupported, signature, binding, expiry, stale and position failures. Generation movement requests a retry; page metadata explains coverage and cost.
Reviewed the R1-R8 trace against the implementation and tests. Independently exercised the focused regression selection, including round-7 cases, under normal and race-enabled execution.

The cursor implementation covers the five declared list tools and their shared helper. Strict artifact-check passed. No daemon, retained snapshot store, durable signing key or indexed query engine was introduced.

HMAC protects token integrity, query/project/root bindings restrict replay, tokens are bounded, and process restart invalidates prior signatures. Pagination remains navigation and introduces no gate or write authorization.

A shared signed cursor plus collection comparison is sufficient for explicit restart semantics. Retained snapshots and durable keys add lifecycle obligations without a current requirement. Revisit if cross-process continuation or indexed selective reads become required.
